interest: Imperial protocol versus American publicity seekers.
overview: This collection of State Department records from decimal file 894.4611 spans June 1934 to March 1938 and documents requests for Imperial audiences with Emperor Hirohito of Japan made by or on behalf of American and foreign dignitaries, journalists, and private travelers. The correspondence details the strict court protocol and standing rules enforced by the Japanese Imperial Household Department and Foreign Ministry, which strictly prohibited granting audiences or interviews to press representatives except in extraordinary cases where individuals were received as industrial leaders rather than journalists. Key episodes documented in the file include Ambassador Joseph C. Grew's handling of audience requests from Hearst correspondent Rudolph Block (writing as Bruno Lessing) and Collier's editor W. B. Courtney; an eccentric incident involving Massachusetts Governor James M. Curley issuing a letter of introduction directly to the Emperor for private travelers Mr. and Mrs. John B. Mickles; and official planning and protocol arrangements for visits by Vice President John Nance Garner and a Congressional delegation, Secretary of War George H. Dern, and Philippine President Manuel L. Quezon.

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports on Hearst journalist Rudolph Block's request for an audience with the Emperor of Japan and the Japanese Foreign Office's refusal.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the Imperial Household bans press audiences, refusing Rudolph Block.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 826 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew regarding Imperial audience request for Rudolph Block

subfiles.about: Rudolph Block asks Ambassador Grew to informally intimate to the Japanese Foreign Office that an Imperial audience request on his behalf would be welcome.
subfiles.summary: Rudolph Block asks Grew to hint to Japan that his audience would be welcome.
subfiles.title: Letter from Rudolph Block to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew proposing audience arrangements

subfiles.about: President Connolly certifies that Rudolph Block is an accredited correspondent for King Features Syndicate and the Hearst Newspapers.
subfiles.summary: J. V. Connolly, President of King Features Syndicate, Inc., issues an official certificate of credentials on behalf of Rudolph Block. The letter certifies that Block is an accredited correspondent for King Features Syndicate and the Hearst Newspapers authorized to submit feature articles and stories from any of his travel assignments.
subfiles.title: Credential letter from J. V. Connolly certifying Rudolph Block as accredited correspondent

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew explains to Rudolph Block that Imperial Household rules and the Emperor's absence preclude an audience.
subfiles.summary: Grew tells Block the press ban stands and the Emperor is away.
subfiles.title: Letter from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew to Rudolph Block declining audience request

subfiles.about: Rudolph Block expresses disappointment at the refusal of an Imperial audience but thanks Ambassador Grew for his efforts.
subfiles.summary: Rudolph Block acknowledges receipt of Ambassador Grew's letter explaining the inability to arrange an Imperial audience with Emperor Hirohito. While expressing disappointment with the decision, Block expresses his sincere appreciation to Grew for the trouble taken on his behalf.
subfiles.title: Letter from Rudolph Block to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew acknowledging audience denial

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting Despatch No. 1423 regarding the desire of Mr. and Mrs. John B. Mickles for an interview with the Emperor of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: the Mickles' request for an audience with the Emperor.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 1423 on Mickles audience request

subfiles.about: Chargé Neville reports on a letter of introduction from Governor James M. Curley addressed to the Emperor of Japan presented by Mrs. Edytha Macy Mickles.
subfiles.summary: Neville reports Governor Curley's letter to 'His Celestial Highness' and Mrs. Mickles's complaints.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1423 from Chargé Edwin L. Neville regarding Governor Curley's letter to the Emperor

subfiles.about: Governor James M. Curley introduces Mr. and Mrs. John B. Mickles to the Emperor of Japan and requests courtesies on their behalf.
subfiles.summary: Governor Curley's letter to the Emperor introducing the Mickles.
subfiles.title: Letter of introduction from Governor James M. Curley to the Emperor of Japan

subfiles.about: Cabot Coville details the complaints and unreasonable demands made by Mrs. Edytha Macy Mickles regarding Embassy services and permits.
subfiles.summary: Coville records Mrs. Mickles's complaints about customs and a Kyoto palace permit.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Cabot Coville regarding complaint of Mrs. Edytha Macy Mickles

subfiles.about: Cabot Coville informs Mrs. Mickles that her Kyoto Imperial Palace permit was processed promptly and will be delivered shortly.
subfiles.summary: Coville tells Mrs. Mickles her Kyoto palace permit is coming.
subfiles.title: Letter from Cabot Coville to Mrs. Edytha Macy Mickles regarding Kyoto Palace permit

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting Telegram No. 170 regarding a proposed Imperial audience for Vice President Garner and Congressional delegates.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Emperor cannot receive Garner's whole party.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Telegram No. 170 on Vice President Garner's audience

subfiles.about: Chargé Neville reports discussions with Japanese officials on an Imperial audience for Vice President Garner and select Congressional leaders.
subfiles.summary: Neville proposes limiting Garner's audience to key congressional leaders.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 170 from Chargé Edwin L. Neville on Imperial audience for Vice President Garner

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording Telegram No. 135 instructing that Secretary of War Dern's visit be treated officially and an audience arranged.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Dern's visit to be official, with an audience.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Telegram No. 135 regarding Secretary of War Dern's visit

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting Telegram No. 149 regarding former Senator Hawes's request that the Speaker of the House accompany Vice President Garner to an Imperial audience.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: request that Speaker Byrns be received with Garner.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Telegram No. 149 regarding audience for Speaker of the House

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a War Department letter conveying President Manuel L. Quezon's desire for an audience with the Emperor of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Quezon seeks an audience with the Emperor, 1937.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for War Department letter on President Quezon's audience request

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording a letter from Secretary of War Woodring renewing President Quezon's request for an Imperial audience in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Woodring renews Quezon's audience request.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Secretary of War Woodring's renewed request for President Quezon

subfiles.about: Secretary of War Woodring outlines President Quezon's revised travel schedule and renews his request for an audience with the Emperor of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Woodring asks State to arrange Quezon's audience in Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of War Harry H. Woodring regarding President Quezon's travel and audience

subfiles.about: Internal State Department routing memorandum noting that the Far Eastern Division handled Collier's audience request.
subfiles.summary: Protocol note on the Collier's audience request.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Division of Protocol to Mr. Duvall on Collier's audience request

subfiles.about: William L. Chenery requests State Department sponsorship for Collier's associate editor W. B. Courtney to receive an Imperial audience in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Collier's asks Hull for Grew to sponsor W. B. Courtney's audience.
subfiles.title: Letter from William L. Chenery to Secretary of State Cordell Hull regarding W. B. Courtney

subfiles.about: Assistant Secretary Messersmith declines departmental sponsorship for Courtney's audience, advising direct application to Ambassador Grew.
subfiles.summary: Messersmith says audience requests are for Grew to decide.
subfiles.title: Letter from Assistant Secretary George S. Messersmith to William L. Chenery declining direct intervention
